brief: A three-storey tower: drawers on the bottom storey and open bins on the top storey.

requirements.evidence: Half bases are stacked at levels 0, 1 and 2 in cells (0,0) and (1,0) and joined with snaps.
There are two drawers at level 0: drawer:0#0,0#cut and drawer:0#1,0#cut.

requirements.requirement: Open bins on the top storey
requirements.evidence: There are two open bins at level 2: bin:0,0,2 and bin:1,0,2 (hex-bin-half-n-full-div2). Neither has a lid or cover.

finish.summary: I built a tower two cells wide and three storeys tall, made of half bases (half-n) at (0,0) and (1,0). The bottom storey has two drawers and the top storey has two open bins. The middle storey is empty. I bolted the joints and capped the open faces except one at 1,0,0;*;150, where a cap would hit the drawer frame. The build check found no rule errors and no collisions between parts. The build has 55 parts in total, and most are end caps. I used half bases because drawers only fit on the cut face of a half base. A full base can't sit on top of a half base, so all three storeys are halves. I added no props because the brief doesn't ask for them.

lines.label: Bin, north half, full depth, 2 compartments
M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
